name: Philip Frankfeld
bio: Philip Frankfeld was the chairman of the Maryland Communist Party, convicted in the 1952 Baltimore Smith Act trial of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the government. He was among the sixteen Smith Act prisoners still behind bars in early 1956 listed in the A. J. Muste–Eleanor Roosevelt amnesty petition.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Benjamin Careathers
bio: Benjamin Careathers was a veteran Black Communist organizer in Pittsburgh, convicted in the western Pennsylvania Smith Act trial. In October 1956 the U.S. Supreme Court threw out the convictions of Careathers, Steve Nelson and their co-defendants because the prosecution had relied on the perjured testimony of the paid informer Joseph Mazzei.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Convicted; conviction vacated by the Supreme Court (1956) over tainted testimony

name: Emanuel Blum
bio: Emanuel Blum was described as 'Indiana's first Smith Act victim,' indicted in 1956 under the Smith Act's membership clause. He charged that he was really being prosecuted for having criticized President Eisenhower over the Korean War rather than for advocating any overthrow of the government.
sentence: Bail reduced from $20,000 to $5,000; awaiting trial

name: John Cyril Hellman
bio: John Cyril Hellman was a Montana Communist and former state director of the Progressive Party, arrested by FBI agents at dawn in Butte in April 1956 under the Smith Act's membership clause. The federal judge in his case, William Murray, publicly rebuked J. Edgar Hoover for the FBI's 'un-American, unfair tactics' in issuing pre-trial press statements.
sentence: Bail set at $20,000, reduced to $5,000; released on property bond

name: Edward E. Strong
bio: Edward E. Strong was a Black Communist leader, one of seven top Massachusetts Communists arrested under the Smith Act on May 29, 1956 and arraigned that June before Judge Bailey Aldrich in Boston.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Geoffrey W. White
bio: Geoffrey W. White was one of seven top Massachusetts Communists arrested under the Smith Act on May 29, 1956 and arraigned in Boston before Judge Bailey Aldrich.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Henry Steinberg
bio: Henry Steinberg was one of the fourteen California Communist leaders convicted in the 1952 Los Angeles Smith Act trial. His conviction was on appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court, which in 1957 reversed the California convictions in the landmark case Yates v. United States.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Convicted 1952; on appeal to the Supreme Court
sentence: Up to five years; on bail pending appeal

name: Margaret Gilbert
bio: Margaret Gilbert was one of four Massachusetts defendants indicted under the state's anti-Communist 'sedition' law for alleged subversive advocacy. The indictments were ordered dismissed in 1956 after the Supreme Court's Nelson decision held that the federal Smith Act preempted state sedition laws.
convicted: Indicted; indictment dismissed 1956 after the Nelson ruling

name: Harry E. Winner
bio: Harry E. Winner was one of four Massachusetts defendants indicted under the state anti-Communist 'sedition' law; the indictments were ordered dismissed in 1956 in the wake of the Supreme Court's Nelson ruling striking down state sedition statutes.
convicted: Indicted; indictment dismissed 1956 after the Nelson ruling
